prerequisites: Intermediate programming skills in a high-level programming language

learning_outcomes.text: The student/graduate describes, identifies and explains the functioning and administration of computer networks and operating systems.
The student/graduate designs, applies, operates and develops relational databases.
The student/graduate identifies, selects and justifies database design principles and models.
The student/graduate designs, builds and develops databases and database systems.
The graduate is able to identify complex problems and examine related issues to develop solving options and implement solutions.
The student/graduate has the knowledge necessary to understand and solve complex problems, and to plan and organize advanced processes in various fields.
The graduate has the ability to apply general rules to specific problems and produce relevant solutions.
The graduate is able to combine diverse information to formulate solutions and generate ideas for developing new products and applications.
To become familiar with the fundamental concepts of concurrency control and database recovery
To become familiar with the fundamental concepts of query optimization
To become familiar with the fundamental concepts of distributed databases and parallel databases
To become familiar with the fundamental concepts of database security
To create ADO.NET applications with data-bound controls
To manage concurrent transactions using pessimistic and optimistic concurrency control mechanisms

syllabus_topics: Data Stream Processing: Azure Stream Analytics, Azure Machine Learning
Windows Forms application using ADO.NET to interact with a SQL Server database
Generic Windows Forms application - configuration file
assessment_rules: To pass, a student must obtain a grade of at least 5 (on a scale from 1 to 10) in the written exam, practical exam, and lab evaluation. To be eligible to take the exam, a student must have attended at least 6 laboratory classes and at least 5 seminar classes.
